title: Calling AI Guard at runtime: the proxy endpoint, the DAS detection API, its host, direction and policy ID, and throttling in the Python SDK

prose.text: Applications reach AI Guard at runtime in one of two ways: as a proxy in front of the LLM provider, or by calling its detection API around their own LLM calls. These calls are not part of the OneAPI configuration API.

prose.label: Proxy mode.
prose.text: {{proxy-paths}} {{proxy-key-header}} The mode itself is described in [[ai-security.ai-guard:proxy-single-destination]].

prose.label: Where the sources disagree.
prose.text: The host differs between Help and the SDK {{divergence:das-host}}, which is open {{gap:host-selection}}. The direction values differ {{divergence:direction-literals}}, open {{gap:direction-aliases}}. Whether execute-policy needs a policy ID differs {{divergence:policy-id-required}}, open {{gap:execute-without-policy-id}}.

prose.label: Throttling.
prose.text: {{throttle-metrics}} {{throttle-hook-name}} {{throttle-hook-skipped}} A test of it is open {{gap:throttle-handling}}.

prose.label: Other entry points.
prose.text: The Anthropic inference-hook endpoint is in [[ai-security.ai-guard.tenant-settings:anthropic-webhook]], and Zscaler's integration examples in [[ai-security.ai-guard.integrations]].

prose.label: What the integration examples say.
prose.text: Zscaler's integration examples use the regional host form {{examples-regional-host}} {{examples-match-sdk}}; they do not show whether the global host also works, so that stays open. They also state, at rank 4, that a policy ID the key cannot use comes back as "Policy not found" in an HTTP 200 with no action ([[ai-security.ai-guard.integrations:soft-failure]]), that a non-UUID transactionId gets HTTP 500 ([[ai-security.ai-guard.integrations:transaction-id-uuid]]), and that resolve-and-execute ignores a policyId in the body ([[ai-security.ai-guard.integrations.google-apigee-proxy:resolve-ignores-policy-id]]); their statement that the API takes only content, direction, transactionId and policyId conflicts with the SDK's `user` field ([[ai-security.ai-guard.integrations.google-apigee-sharedflow:api-fields]]). The native LiteLLM guardrail defaults to execute-policy with `policy_id` optional ([[ai-security.ai-guard.integrations.litellm:native-endpoint]]).

checks.do: That the application calls AI Guard on both the prompt and the response, and treats a failed inspection explicitly rather than passing content through.
Which host the client uses: Help's global api.zseclipse.net or the SDK's api.<cloud>.zseclipse.net (cloud us1 unless set); pin it with the override when they differ.
That direction is IN for prompts and OUT for responses when using the SDK, and that execute-policy calls carry a policy ID.
That the caller reads throttlingDetails and waits retryAfterMillis itself; at the pin the SDK's helper does not act on it.

proxy-paths.statement: In proxy mode the application keeps each provider's own request path but sends it to `https://proxy.zseclipse.net`; the proxy page lists Anthropic (`/v1/messages`), AWS Bedrock Agent, AWS Bedrock Anthropic, AWS Bedrock Invoke, Azure Foundry (`/openai/v1/chat/completions`), Google Gemini, Google Vertex and OpenAI (`/v1/chat/completions`).

quotes: Anthropic Provider-specific upstream in AI Guard /v1/messages
AWS Bedrock Agent Provider-specific upstream in AI Guard /agents/<AGENT_ID>/agentAliases/<AGENT_ALIAS_ID>/sessions/<SESSION_ID>/text
AWS Bedrock Anthropic Provider-specific upstream in AI Guard /model/anthropic.<MODEL>/invoke
AWS Bedrock Invoke Provider-specific upstream in AI Guard /model/<MODEL>/converse
OpenAI Provider-specific upstream in AI Guard /v1/chat/completions
When configuring a proxy for Zscaler, use the following base URL endpoint: https://proxy.zseclipse.net

proxy-key-header.statement: A proxy-mode request authenticates to AI Guard with the AI Guard application key in an `X-ApiKey` header; the Anthropic example also sends an `anthropic-version` header giving the API version in use.

quotes: X-ApiKey: The AI Guard application key which is mandatory for authentication.

two-endpoints.statement: DAS mode has two endpoints: `execute-policy` checks content against one specific policy ID, for deterministic use of a known policy; `resolve-and-execute-policy` sends no policy ID and lets AI Guard resolve and apply the matching policy.

quotes: There are two primary endpoints for DAS/API mode:
You want to explicitly reference a specific AI Guard policy.
You want AI Guard to resolve which policy should match.
AI Guard resolves and applies the appropriate policy.
You want deterministic use of one exact policy.

resolve-requirements.statement: Resolve-and-execute needs DAS/API policies to exist in AI Guard; AI Guard evaluates them and determines the matching one, so several DAS/API policies may apply and the application should not hard-code a single policy ID.

quotes: DAS/API policies must exist in AI Guard.
AI Guard evaluates those policies and determines the matching policy.
The application should not hard-code a single policy ID.

help-host.statement: The DAS page calls both endpoints on the host `https://api.zseclipse.net`, authenticating with the AI Guard API key as a Bearer token and sending `direction` and `content` in the body.

both-directions.statement: The application should inspect both sides: the prompt before it is sent to the model and the response before it is shown to the user; skipping the response call gives up output enforcement.

quotes: The prompt before it is sent to the model.
The response before it is shown back to the user.
Do not bypass the response-side call if output enforcement is required.

failure-handling.statement: The DAS page advises a short request timeout for the inspection call, explicit handling of AI Guard failures, error handling for failed inspections and return-message wording for blocked inspections in the application, and logging blocked events without exposing sensitive content broadly.

quotes: Use a short request timeout for AI Guard inspection.
Log blocked events safely without exposing sensitive content broadly.
Return message verbiage for blocked inspections.

sdk-legacy-client.statement: In the Python SDK the detection endpoints are not exposed through OneAPI: they are called with `LegacyAIGuardClient` and an AI Guard API key, while every other AI Guard resource is OneAPI-only through `ZscalerClient`.

quotes: They must be called with :class:`~zscaler.oneapi_client.LegacyAIGuardClient`, which
authenticates with an AI Guard API key against ``https://api.<cloud>.zseclipse.net``.
Every other AI Guard resource -- detection policies, policy match rules, LLM
providers, LLM applications and their credentials -- is **OneAPI only** and is

sdk-host.statement: The SDK's legacy client sends detection calls to `https://api.<cloud>.zseclipse.net`, taking the cloud from the config's `cloud`, else `AIGUARD_CLOUD`, else `us1`; an `override_url` or `AIGUARD_OVERRIDE_URL` replaces the whole base URL.

quotes: (``AIGUARD_CLOUD`` for the cloud, ``AIGUARD_OVERRIDE_URL`` to override the base URL).
authenticates with an AI Guard API key against ``https://api.<cloud>.zseclipse.net``.

sdk-bearer.statement: The legacy helper sets an Authorization header carrying the API key as a Bearer token on each detection request; detection calls are dispatched through it since release 1.9.44, which fixed them falling through to the standard OneAPI session without the AI Guard API key.

quotes: Fixed AI Guard policy detection requests not being dispatched through the legacy AI Guard client. `execute_policy` and `resolve_and_execute_policy` fell through to the standard OneAPI session and were sent without the AI Guard API key.

sdk-direction-doc.statement: The SDK documents `direction` as `IN` or `OUT` for both detection methods, and each method's minimal-payload example passes `direction="IN"`.

quotes: direction (str): The direction of the content ('IN' or 'OUT')
direction (str): The direction of the content ('IN' or 'OUT')

sdk-policy-id-optional.statement: `execute_policy` takes `policy_id` as optional and puts `policyId` in the body only when it is given; `transactionId` is likewise added only when given.

resolve-user-headers.statement: `resolve_and_execute_policy` accepts an optional `user` since release 1.10.0, recorded on the detection event so the user appears on the dashboard, and optional extra `headers` since release 1.10.1, which are merged into the request and let a caller send the tenant's configured custom request headers, including the one AI Guard reads a conversation ID from to correlate multi-turn interactions.

quotes: argument to AI Guard `resolve_and_execute_policy`. The end-user identity is recorded on the
detection event so the user surfaces on the dashboard.
Added an optional `headers` argument to AI Guard `resolve_and_execute_policy`.
merged into the request, which lets a caller send the tenant's configured custom request headers
including the one AI Guard reads the conversation ID from, so multi-turn interactions can be

response-fields.statement: The SDK's response models read `transactionId`, `statusCode`, `errorMsg`, `detectorErrorCount`, `action`, `severity`, `direction`, a map of per-detector `detectorResponses` (each with `triggered`, `action`, `severity`, `latency` and an optional `contentHash`), and a list of `throttlingDetails` with `rlcId`, `metric` and `retryAfterMillis`.

quotes: self.transaction_id = config["transactionId"] if "transactionId" in config else None
self.status_code = config["statusCode"] if "statusCode" in config else None
self.error_msg = config["errorMsg"] if "errorMsg" in config else None
self.detector_error_count = config["detectorErrorCount"] if "detectorErrorCount" in config else None
self.action = config["action"] if "action" in config else None
self.severity = config["severity"] if "severity" in config else None
self.direction = config["direction"] if "direction" in config else None
config["throttlingDetails"] if "throttlingDetails" in config else [], RateLimitThrottlingDetail
self.triggered = config["triggered"] if "triggered" in config else None
self.latency = config["latency"] if "latency" in config else None
self.action = config["action"] if "action" in config else None
self.severity = config["severity"] if "severity" in config else None
self.rlc_id = config["rlcId"] if "rlcId" in config else None
self.metric = config["metric"] if "metric" in config else None
self.retry_after_millis = config["retryAfterMillis"] if "retryAfterMillis" in config else None

resolve-policy-fields.statement: The resolve-and-execute response model also reads `policyId`, `policyName` and `policyVersion`, naming the policy AI Guard resolved.

quotes: self.policy_id = config["policyId"] if "policyId" in config else None
self.policy_name = config["policyName"] if "policyName" in config else None
self.policy_version = config["policyVersion"] if "policyVersion" in config else None

throttle-metrics.statement: The legacy helper's throttling handler treats a `metric` of `rq` as a request-count limit and `cs` as a content-size limit, sleeps for the longest retry-after value when `auto_retry_on_rate_limit` is on (the default), and makes later requests wait until the recorded limit resets.

throttle-hook-name.statement: The detection methods pass a response's throttling details to `_handle_throttling_details` on the request executor's `zguard_legacy_client` only if the request executor has an attribute of that name; the request executor stores the legacy helper as `aiguard_legacy_client`.

throttle-hook-skipped.statement: At the pin, a throttled detection response never reaches the helper's handler: the SDK neither sleeps on `retryAfterMillis` nor delays later requests, so a caller has to read `throttlingDetails` and wait itself.
throttle-hook-skipped.conditions: Follows from Python `hasattr` on an attribute the request executor never sets: a search of the package finds no other `zguard_legacy_client` and no `__getattr__` on the executor. Not exercised against a live endpoint.

examples-regional-host.statement: Zscaler's integration examples build the DAS host from the cloud name as `https://api.{cloud}.zseclipse.net` (the repository's agent notes and the Cursor, n8n and Azure AI Gateway READMEs); the CI scanner treats a blank cloud as `us1` because an empty one yields `api..zseclipse.net`.

quotes: Used to build the API URL: `https://api.{cloud}.zseclipse.net`.
# Azure AI Gateway + Zscaler AI Guard Integration
# becomes api..zseclipse.net. Treat blank like unset.

examples-match-sdk.statement: That host form matches the SDK's regional host, not the global host the Help DAS page uses.
examples-match-sdk.conditions: A comparison of the host strings in examples-regional-host, sdk-host and help-host; no example document states the comparison itself.

das-host.summary: Which host serves the DAS detection endpoints.

positions.says: Help calls both endpoints on the global host api.zseclipse.net.
The Python SDK builds a per-cloud host, api.<cloud>.zseclipse.net, with cloud us1 unless configured.

das-host.impact: A client following one source may call a host the other source does not use; no source says whether both hosts accept the calls or which is preferred. The SDK's override URL can pin the Help host.

direction-literals.summary: Which values the direction field takes.

positions.says: The Python SDK documents IN or OUT.

quotes: direction (str): The direction of the content ('IN' or 'OUT')

positions.says: The DAS Help page's examples pass "request" and "response", and its prose speaks of the outbound prompt and the inbound response.

quotes: direction should indicate whether this is the outbound prompt or inbound response.

direction-literals.impact: A request built from the Help examples may send values the SDK does not document; whether the API accepts both sets is unknown.

policy-id-required.summary: Whether execute-policy requires a policy ID.

positions.says: The DAS Help page says policyId is required for execute-policy.
The Python SDK makes policy_id optional and omits policyId when it is not given.

policy-id-required.impact: An SDK call to execute_policy without a policy ID sends a request Help calls invalid; resolve_and_execute_policy is the documented call when no ID is intended.

host-selection.title: Which DAS host to use: the global api.zseclipse.net or api.<cloud>.zseclipse.net
host-selection.detail: Static sources do not establish whether the global and regional hosts both work, whether one is preferred, or whether the regional form is stale. The SDK and Zscaler's integration examples build the regional form (examples-regional-host); the help names the global host. An upstream issue (zguard-ai-integrations#10) reports the regional policy-resolution host no longer working and the global host working; it is an issue report, not a specification.
host-selection.blocks: which host a DAS client should be configured with

direction-aliases.title: Whether the detection API accepts request and response as direction values
direction-aliases.detail: Whether the live API accepts both IN/OUT and request/response, normalizes one to the other, or treats the Help values as pseudocode is unverified.
direction-aliases.blocks: building a valid DAS request from the Help page

execute-without-policy-id.title: What execute-policy does without a policy ID
execute-without-policy-id.detail: It is unclear whether the server rejects execute-policy without policyId, falls back to resolution, or whether the SDK's optional parameter exists only for payload-building convenience.
execute-without-policy-id.blocks: answers on SDK execute_policy calls that pass no policy_id

throttle-handling.title: Whether the SDK acts on detection throttling details
throttle-handling.detail: The former static concern had two halves. The dispatch and Bearer-header half is resolved in source (sdk-bearer, release 1.9.44). The throttling half remains: the detection methods look for zguard_legacy_client while the executor stores aiguard_legacy_client (throttle-hook-name), so the helper's handler looks unreachable (throttle-hook-skipped). No unit test or live call has confirmed it.
throttle-handling.blocks: whether SDK users get automatic back-off on detection throttling
